Yesterday, the U.S. government released an updated list of prohibited foreign-manufactured imports, adding a new "advanced robotic devices" category. A Federal Communications Commission (FCC) spokesperson confirmed today that the ban also applies to robot vacuum cleaners.

The robot vacuum ban affects well-known brands such as Roomba and Roborock, but you can continue to use your existing devices

When the Trump administration announced yesterday a ban on "advanced robotic devices" entering the United States, media attention focused on humanoid robots. Yet espionage doesn't necessarily require legs — and the FCC's robot ban is no exception. FCC Director of Media Relations Katie Gorscak confirmed to The Verge that the ban also covers robot vacuum cleaners. Your existing Roomba at home is not the target of the ban, and companies can still import and sell approved models. However, the government claims future foreign robots will pose a threat to national security, and even robot vacuum companies have suddenly been required to commit to manufacturing within the United States.

The FCC stated that advanced robotic devices pose a risk to national security, and the regulations also apply to seemingly harmless products such as robot vacuum cleaners and robotic lawn mowers.

Unless a product receives explicit approval, or is for example manufactured in the United States, it will not be allowed to be sold domestically.

The ban is expected to deal an especially heavy blow to the robot vacuum market, as top brands such as Roomba, Roborock, and Ecovacs are all owned by Chinese companies.

If you already own the relevant products, you can still continue to use them today — the FCC won't show up at your door to confiscate your robot vacuum.

However, depending on how the ban is enforced, the robot vacuum market could undergo dramatic changes in a short period of time. If you feel like you've seen this before, that's completely normal, because this ban is very similar to the wireless router ban implemented a few months ago.

Will you continue to use your existing robot vacuum? Why? Feel free to share with us in the comments section.
